He did not include a caption and instead tagged the Vuori brand's Instagram account. Gerber died Sept. 20 at age 27 while staying at a rehabilitation facility, according to records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The model's cause of death was "deferred," according to online records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The medical examiner told Fox News Digital that "the investigation is still ongoing and there is limited information available." Santa Monica Police Department officials are investigating the death as "a suspected overdose," according to a release from the department. A representative for the family told Fox News Digital, "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time." Gerber’s post was one of several instances in which he publicly documented his recovery journey. In recent years, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber spoke candidly about depression, panic attacks, addiction and the challenges of seeking treatment. During a 2023 episode of the "Studio 22" podcast, Gerber discussed his experiences with depression and other mental health challenges. "[Mental health] is an issue. It is such a big part of my life. It’s a 24/7 job, and there’s so much to it," he said. "That’s really what I want to do is help people, whether you’re depressed, you’re struggling with something that is having a negative effect on your body," he continued. "I mean it could be anything, and there’s no judgment." Gerber said he hoped his experiences could help other people avoid making similar mistakes. "I’ve seen a lot of stuff, and I’ve learned a lot of things," he said. "What I hope I can do is have made the mistakes for some other people, so they don’t have to make the same mistakes that I made." He added, "I’m proud that something I created has inspired others and started a bigger movement around openness and healing." articles.title: Ferran Torres: "Marcar gol siempre es adictivo, más como delantero"
articles.standfirst: El autor del gol de España en la final del Mundial ha sido el invitado de Pablo Motos este lunes en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.summary: El autor del gol de España en la final del Mundial ha sido el invitado de Pablo Motos este lunes en 'El Hormiguero'
articles.body: 'El Hormiguero' ha empezado la se mana con la visita del futbolista Ferran Torres, el autor del gol de España en la final del Mundial, quien ha contado cómo vivió ese momento y todo lo que ha sobrevenido desde entonces en su vida tras firmar uno de los goles más importantes del fútbol español. PABLO MOTOS. ¡Qué recibimiento! ¡Qué bonito que la gente te quiera tanto! FERRAN TORRES. Muy bonito. Poder haber hecho feliz a todo nuestro país, el mejor del mundo, es increíble. PABLO MOTOS. Yo soy la única persona que no vio el mundial, pero te quiero también mucho. Además, creo que soy un talismán. No vi el de Iniesta y ganamos, y no vi este y también. Creo que ya no debo verlo nunca más FERRAN TORRES. Pues quizá podrías probar a verlo, a ver qué pasa, aunque sé que no es que no hayas visto la final, sino que no has visto ningún partido. PABLO MOTOS. Qué importante es la mentalidad ganadora en la competición FERRAN TORRES. Si algo he aprendido a lo largo de estos años es que si hablan de ti, para bien o para mal, es que algo más grande que ellos estás haciendo. Yo creo en el destino, creo que ese balón estaba allí para mí, y que no fue un gol mío, sino que sentí la fuerza de todos los españoles ayudándome a marcar ese gol. PABLO MOTOS. Intenta describir tus pensamientos desde que viste el balón hasta que marcaste el gol FERRAN TORRES. Cuando vi que Lamine le pasó la pelota a Porro hacia detrás, yo, no sé por qué, empecé a dar pasitos hacia delante, hacia la portería. Cuando le llegó el balón a Nico, sentí que estaba en una isla, que solo estaba yo. Tuve la sensación de que no había nadie más que el balón y yo, sentí un silencio absoluto durante un segundo, y después ya estaba tirando a portería. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Cuántas veces has visto las imágenes del gol? FERRAN TORRES. Millones, yo creo que mínimo una vez al día lo vuelvo a ver. Fue un chute tan fuerte de adrenalina en el momento de marcar que, después de la celebración, no conseguía recordar cómo había sido. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Qué da más gusto, meter gol o callar las bocas? FERRAN TORRES. En ese momento del Mundial meter el gol, pero a mí me va el salseo y dejar un par de titulares siempre me gusta. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Ya no te saben el resto de goles que metes igual que el del Mundial? FERRAN TORRES. Ese gol no se puede comparar con nada en el mundo, pero sí que he aprendido que no hay que venirse arriba demasiado, igual que tampoco hay que venirse abajo cuando las cosas no salen. Marcar gol siempre es adictivo, más como delantero. PABLO MOTOS. Te convertiste en el hombre más deseado de España, sobre todo después del audio viral de '¡Oh, Ferran!', ¿cómo te enteraste? FERRAN TORRES. Yo estaba en Estados Unidos en una burbuja, concentrado con la misma gente y al margen de todo. Hasta después de la Rua no me di cuenta del revuelo que estaba generando el vídeo viral de '¡Oh, Ferran!'. La verdad es que me da muchísima vergüenza. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Dónde estabas cuando el gol de Iniesta? FERRAN TORRES. Estaba en el restaurante de un amigo y acabé en la fuente del pueblo bañándome en calzoncillos. Tenía 10 años. Nunca pensaba que podría hacer yo algo parecido. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Qué tal te va en París? FERRAN TORRES. Me estoy adaptando bien, pero, por ejemplo, esta semana ha sido muy dura, porque estoy en plena mudanza de Barcelona a París. Es difícil, se echa mucho de menos a la gente, a tu país. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Cómo es Luis Enrique? FERRAN TORRES. Es súper natural. Si te tiene que decir algo te lo va a decir, sea bueno o malo.Es una persona muy fiel a lo suyo y a los suyos. Siempre le he tenido como un padre futbolístico y creo que va a saber sacar todo mi potencial. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Cómo llevas lo de perder? FERRAN TORRES. Tengo peor perder con mi gente cercana jugando, por ejemplo, a un juego de mesa que en un partido, que controlo más mis impulsos. Lo pago con quienes más quiero y luego, claro, tengo que disculparme. PABLO MOTOS. Dices que tu hermana es tu mayor apoyo, ¿qué ha hecho por ti? FERRAN TORRES. Somos el mayor amor-odio. Creo que ese es el verdadero amor. El amor no es solo cosas bonitas, también discusiones y peleas. Ella ha sacrificado su vida y su futuro para proteger el mío; trabaja conmigo. Aprovecho para saludarla y pedirle perdón, que la última vez que hablamos discutimos.

articles.title: National Park Service director calls Yellowstone's wild bison recovery an 'incredible conservation story'
articles.summary: Over 600 Yellowstone bison have been transferred to 29 tribes across 13 states since 2019 through a landmark conservation program partnership.
articles.body: A little more than a century ago, Yellowstone's bison were hanging on by a thread. Today, thousands of them roam the park. And the conservation challenge has shifted from simply saving the herd to figuring out how to manage a thriving one. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS During an interview with OutKick OutDoors, Jessica Bowron, acting director of the National Park Service, called the recovery an "incredible conservation story." After millions of bison once roamed the Great Plains, the animals were nearly wiped out across their historic range. Rebuilding those populations, Bowron said, has taken decades of careful scientific work and cooperation among the Park Service and its Tribal, state, local and federal partners. "To show up at Yellowstone today and have the experience as a visitor of seeing a wild bison in a functioning ecosystem, I don't know that we could have predicted that 100 years ago," Bowron said. That's a pretty remarkable turnaround. And now, Yellowstone's bison are helping build conservation herds far beyond the park itself. Yellowstone bison are finding new homes Through the Bison Conservation Transfer Program, Yellowstone works with Tribal partners to relocate live bison that have completed the necessary quarantine process. Since 2019, more than 600 bison have been transferred to 29 tribes across 13 states, according to Bowron. More than 200 were transferred in 2026 alone. "This is one of the coolest parts of this entire conservation effort," Bowron said. Once the animals are transferred, she explained, each tribe can manage its herd according to its own priorities and sovereignty. "It's a great example of how we're able to establish and expand conservation herds through that kind of partnership," Bowron said. But conservation success doesn't mean the work is finished. In some places, rebuilding the population remains the goal. At Yellowstone, Bowron said the challenge now is largely about managing the healthy herd that's already there. "I think at Yellowstone, we're in the latter — figuring out how to successfully manage the herd that we have with all of our partners," she said. At the same time, the Park Service continues to pursue live-transfer opportunities with tribes interested in establishing or expanding conservation herds. A conservation problem you want to have The Yellowstone story is also a reminder that conservation wins don't happen overnight. Bowron said rebuilding bison populations has taken decades of scientific monitoring and cooperation among Tribal, state, local and federal partners. WHY TED TURNER'S APPROACH TO CONSERVATION IS THE MINDSET AMERICA DESPERATELY NEEDS RIGHT NOW And even after a species rebounds, the work changes rather than disappears. For generations, the question was whether wild bison could survive at all in places like Yellowstone. Now, wildlife managers are dealing with a very different question: What do you do when the comeback works? Bison don't care where Yellowstone's boundary lines are drawn. They move across a massive landscape, meaning managing a successful herd requires cooperation among the Park Service and the many communities and agencies surrounding it. But the fact that there is a healthy herd to manage — and enough animals to help establish conservation herds elsewhere — would have been difficult to imagine a century ago. For anyone who's ever sat in Yellowstone traffic because a bison decided the middle of the road belonged to him, it might be easy to forget just how close America came to losing that experience entirely. articles.body: Taylor Swift will be the first recipient of the MTV Video Music Awards artist-director honours at this year's awards ceremony, a newly created award recognizing musicians whose work behind the camera has contributed to music video production and visual storytelling, CBS and MTV said on Monday.The television networks said the honor for the 14-time Grammy winner "celebrates a sustained and influential body of work from artists who have pushed creative boundaries and developed a clear directorial voice."Taylor Swift awarded MTV Video Music Awards Artist-Director honorThe singer-songwriter, a seven-time VMA Best Director nominee and four-time winner, has earned recognition for videos and films including "The Fate of Ophelia," "Opalite," and "Anti-Hero."Taylor Swift to beome most-awarded artist in VMA historyTaylor Swift will once again break records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Currently, Swift is tied with Beyoncé for the title of most-awarded musician in VMA history. They have 30 each. (Eminem is the male artist with the most VMAs, with 15.) Blackpink’s LISA has four and Shakira, Tate McRae, GENER8ION and Yung Lean are tied for three.Rounding out the artist of the year category nominees are Grande, Mars, Carpenter and Morgan Wallen, in addition to Madonna and Swift.What's new this year?This year’s Video Music Awards features 26 first-time nominees, which include GENER8ION and Yung Lean (for their “Storm” collaboration) and the K-pop boy band CORTIS and viral “Boston” singer Stella Lefty with two each. Other notable first-time nominees include Don Toliver, Kali Uchis, Noah Kahan, Olivia Dean, Tucker Wetmore and Sienna Spiro.The best dance category has returned for the first time in seven years. Nominees include McRae’s “Nobody’s Girl,” Bebe Rexha and Faithless’ “New Religion,” Harry Styles’ “Aperture,” Lady Gaga and Doechii’s “Runway,” Madonna’s “Confessions II — The Film,” PinkPantheress’ “Stateside” with Larsson and Slayyyter’s “Dance …”Who is performing at the 2026 MTV VMAs?Madonna will open the show. articles.standfirst: Reunião de seis cantoras em inédito show no Rio de Janeiro reforça onda de homenagens ao artista, voz de uma pessoa vitoriosa e muitas vezes transgressora.
articles.summary: Reunião de seis cantoras em inédito show no Rio de Janeiro reforça onda de homenagens ao artista, voz de uma pessoa vitoriosa e muitas vezes transgressora.
articles.body:
Ney Matogrosso tem sido celebrado em shows geralmente criados por artistas associados ao universo LGBTQIA+ — Foto: David LaChapelle / Divulgação

♬ No próximo domingo, 27 de setembro, às 18h, seis cantoras da geração dos anos 2010 – Juliana Linhares, Linn da Quebrada, MC Tha, Melly, Tássia Reis e Xênia França – estarão juntas pela primeira vez no palco em show em tributo a Ney Matogrosso .

Inédito, o espetáculo “Eu prefiro ser – Uma homenagem a Ney Matogrosso” acontece nos Arcos da Lapa, cartão-postal do Centro da cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ), e fecha a Semana de Arte do Rio dentro da programação do festival promovido pelo Solar em homenagem ao cantor com exposição em cartaz desde junho.

Pela reunião das seis cantoras, o show já seria uma notícia. Contudo, o tributo do Solar ao artista está longe de ser um ato isolado, se juntando a uma série de homenagens que vem sendo prestadas a Ney Matogrosso ao longo desde ano de 2026 no Brasil e eventualmente até em Portugal.

Em fevereiro, duas semanas antes de o cantor e ator Fitti estrear em São Paulo (SP) o show em que canta o repertório de Ney Matogrosso com estética teatral, a escola de samba Imperatriz Leopoldinense sobressaiu no Carnaval do Rio de Janeiro ao desfilar com o enredo “Camaleônico” em reverência ao artista.

Em junho, o cantor César Soares abriu a temporada de verão da Casa da Música na cidade do Porto, em Portugal, com show em que celebrou Ney.

Em julho, o cantor Gustavus apresentou o show “Eu bandoleiro – Um tributo a Ney Matogrosso” no teatro do Sesc de Passo Fundo (RS).

Em agosto, mês em que Ney completou 85 anos, a ginasta Flávia Soares apresentou a série solo da esportista para a temporada 2026 com coreografia inspirada na música “Homem com H” (Antônio Barros, 1974), um dos maiores sucessos de Ney desde que a composição foi regravada pelo cantor em 1981.

Já neste mês de setembro, o ator e cantor Fabiano Medeiros reapresentou em São José dos Campos (SP) o show “Pura alquimia”, com o qual vem percorrendo algumas cidades do Brasil desde 2025, com intenção de celebrar a estética libertária de Ney em clima psicodélico.

Tantos tributos sucessivos não são mera coincidência. Aos 85 anos, Ney Matogrosso já se torna uma lenda viva da MPB, por mais que o cantor recuse essa aura e haja com naturalidade, e sem qualquer traço de estrelismo, na vida e nos palcos. Ney sempre foi uma voz e um símbolo de liberdade, de ousadia, de transgressão.

Não por acaso, os tributos ao cantor muitas vezes partem de artistas ligados ao universo LGBTQIA+. À medida em que Ney foi envelhecendo sem se tornar um cantor senhoril em cena ou fora de cena, essa chama libertária se alastra por um país ainda (hipocritamente) conservador sob prisma moral.

Ney Matogrosso tem a voz de uma pessoa vitoriosa que venceu na vida dizendo não, seguindo o próprio caminho e o próprio instinto, jogando sementes nos campos da mente . Como o personagem-título da música “Bandolero” (Luhli e Lucina, 1978), gravada pelo cantor no álbum “Feitiço” (1978), Ney Matogrosso é encanto, magia, sonho, fantasia quando sobe no palco.

Ney é um artista senhor da cena. Tanto que Ney sempre se agigantou mais nos palcos do que nos discos, ainda que a obra fonográfica do cantor seja luminosa, quase irretocável, tendo sido, também ela, a discografia, um símbolo da liberdade que norteia o artista em 53 anos de carreira.

Por isso, Ney Matogrosso é cada vez mais alvo de tributos. Ney Matogrosso é o cantor que muitos preferiam ser...

articles.title: Sylvester Stallone reveals what he said to Trump after surprise Hollywood ambassador appointment
articles.summary: Sylvester Stallone says he learned about Trump's Hollywood ambassador appointment while watching TV and later told the president it was impossible.
articles.body: Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced his appointment as a special ambassador to Hollywood. Days before his second inauguration in January 2025, Trump shared a post on his platform Truth Social in which he named Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as "Special Envoys," describing the role as a way for the three actors to serve as his "eyes and ears" in Hollywood and advise him on efforts to bring film and television production back to the U.S. During a recent interview with The Sunday Times, the 80-year-old "Rocky" star recalled that he found out about the appointment while watching television. SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!' "I was watching TV one night, and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, ‘This is not possible,'" Stallone said. Stallone told the outlet that he was hesitant about taking on the role because he didn't believe it was feasible. When asked if he had reservations after Trump's announcement, Stallone said, "Yes. Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states." 'AMERICAN IDOL' DITCHES HOLLYWOOD FOR GEORGIA AFTER TWO DECADES AS CALIFORNIA LOSES ANOTHER PRODUCTION "They have their little kingdoms," he continued. "You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people. No, it won’t work." The "Tulsa King" star recalled that he later explained his reasoning to Trump. "I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible," Stallone said. "Hollywood works, and it will evolve." "It’s corporate, and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance," he added. 'I PLAY ROCKY' REVIVES THE GAMBLE THAT MADE SYLVESTER STALLONE A SUPERSTAR In his original post on Jan. 16, 2025, Trump wrote, "It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California." "They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!" he continued. "These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!" DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON REJECTS HOLLYWOOD’S POLITICAL OBSESSION, BLASTS CELEBRITY ATTACK CULTURE At the time, Gibson, 70, shared that he was caught off-guard by Trump's announcement and did not have previous knowledge about his presidential appointment. "I got the tweet at the same time as all of you and was just as surprised," he told Variety in January 2025. "Nevertheless, I heed the call. My duty as a citizen is to give any help and insight I can." "Any chance the position comes with an Ambassador’s residence?" Gibson joked. Though Stallone may not have been onboard with his role as a special Hollywood ambassador, the action star appears to have a friendly relationship with Trump and heaped praise on the president during a speech following his victory in the November 2024 election. Days after the election, Stallone introduced Trump at the America First Policy Institute Gala held at the president-elect's Mar-A-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida. "We’re in the presence of a really mythical character," Stallone said of Trump. "I love mythology. And this individual does not exist on this planet. Nobody in the world could have pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe." "When George Washington defended his country, he had no idea that he was gonna change the world," he added. "Because without him, you could imagine what the world would look like. Guess what? We got the second George Washington." Stallone was later selected as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree, with Trump personally naming him among that year’s recipients alongside George Strait, KISS, Gloria Gaynor and Michael Crawford. The actor has backed Republicans, including John McCain and Trump, but his political history has not been strictly partisan. Over the years, Stallone has made financial contributions to both political parties, donating to various Democratic candidates and committees, including former President Joe Biden and the Democratic National Committee, as well as Republican campaigns. Meanwhile, Voight, who is a staunch supporter of Trump, appears to have embraced his role as a special ambassador. He has met with the White House and advocated for policies aimed at bringing film and TV production back to the U.S., especially a federal film tax incentive. articles.title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ influencer Clavicular charged with rape in Massachusetts
articles.summary: The “looksmaxxing” personality known as Clavicular has been charged with rape in Massachusetts, online court records show.
articles.body:
The "looksmaxxing" personality known as Clavicular has been charged with rape in Massachusetts, online court records show.

The charges listed against Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, are one count of rape, one count of drugging someone for sexual intercourse, and one count of procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old, according to the records.

The charges were filed Sept. 8, and the alleged offenses occurred May 23, 2025, the records indicate. More details about the allegations were not immediately available.

Online court records did not show an attorney who could speak on his behalf Monday night.

The Bulwark first reported the charges. A representative for Clavicular, Mitchell Jackson, said the outlet was "exaggerating" in its report and that Clavicular had not been served with an arrest warrant.

"Braden Peters has not been physically served. As usual the Bulwark is exaggerating," Jackson said in a text message Monday night.

An email to the general mailbox of The Bulwark seeking comment was not immediately returned late Monday.

An arraignment was scheduled for Oct. 14, according to the court records.

Clavicular has gained internet fame — and notoriety — for a trend among young men known as " looksmaxxing, " which Meriam-Webster Dictionary recently called, "The practice of taking one or more sometimes extreme or dangerous measures intended to increase one's physical attractiveness."

He has been known for "bone smashing," or using a hammer to intentionally break facial bones so they grow back stronger or looking better. The trend has been called potentially unhealthy and dangerous by experts .

Clavicular in April was sued by a teenage influencer in Florida who accused him of battery.

Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, who online is known as Alorah or Alorah Ziva, filed a lawsuit in Miami-Dade County that alleged that in 2025 he arranged for her to go to Cape Cod, Massachusetts, gave her vodka until she was drunk, and then had sex with her while she was intoxicated, NBC South Florida reported .

Online court records do not indicate whether the charges of rape, drugging or procurement of alcohol to someone under 21 are related to the allegations in the lawsuit.

Clavicular's attorney at the time said that he denies the allegations and "intends to vigorously defend himself," according to the news station.

Clavicular and two other people in April were also charged in Florida with shooting at an alligator. He and another person pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public and were given six months of probation and ordered to serve 20 hours of community service, according to NBC South Florida .

He was also hospitalized in April in Miami after a suspected overdose . He said in a livestream at the time after being released from the hospital that, "I ain't gonna be doing any more substances for a little while, hopefully for forever."

articles.title: Apple’s first live music venue is opening beneath its UK headquarters
articles.summary: Apple is preparing to open a new “state-of-the-art” 600-capacity live music venue in the UK for hosting performances, recording sessions, and video broadcasts.
articles.body: Apple is preparing to open a new “state-of-the-art” live music venue in the UK, a 600-capacity space for hosting performances, recording sessions, and video broadcasts. The venue, called Apple Music Hall, is located underneath Apple’s European headquarters in London’s iconic Battersea Power Station, and is set to open next week on September 28th. Details about the opening show have yet to be announced. “Apple’s deep love for music dates all the way back to the very beginning, from the launch of the iPod to the long-running iTunes Music Festival to the debut of Apple Music,” said Oliver Schusser, Apple’s vice president of Apple Music and International Content. “Today, with the opening of Apple Music Hall, we are once again taking an unprecedented step further in our commitment to artists and fans by supporting live music in ways only Apple can do.” [Image: [Image: [Image: The limited capacity and layout is “designed intentionally to close the gap between intimacy and production value,” according to Apple’s announcement, with seating that feels close to the performer while providing artists with a 38-foot-wide stage that can be reconfigured to their needs. Apple Music Hall has a 48-speaker spatial sound system positioned around the audience, is hardwired for 16 or more broadcast cameras, and includes two dedicated recording and mixing studios behind the stage that allow it to operate as a full production facility. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The performance space is opening alongside new Apple Music radio studios in Battersea, with Apple announcing that all of its London-based hosts and shows will now broadcast from the facility. “We’re always looking for new opportunities to connect the artists and the fans because we are fans,” said Apple Music’s global creative director, Zane Lowe. “Great music and memories will be made at Apple Music Hall.” [Media: Apple Music Hall marks the company’s return to London’s music scene, having previously run the iTunes Music Festival in England’s capital city for a decade — hosting acts like One Direction, Lady Gaga, Elton John, and Adele at intimate local venues — before its cancellation in 2017. Battersea Power Station, a decommissioned Art Deco facility that reopened in 2022, also has its own roots in music history, having appeared on the cover of Pink Floyd’s Animals album.

articles.title: Why is Princess Diana's brother making new claims about King Charles nearly 30 years after her death?
articles.summary: A new book about Diana and an accompanying BBC interview contain new claims from Earl Spencer about King Charles.
articles.body:
It's been nearly 30 years since Princess Diana died in a car accident in Paris. Yet revelations from the days that followed are still making headlines globally, thanks to a book ( Swan Song, released today) written by her brother, Earl Spencer.

Last week, an excerpt from the book prompted the British royal family to break its "never complain, never explain" mantra and issue a statement challenging Spencer's assertion that King Charles III "sounded giddily elated" on a phone call shortly after Diana's death on Aug. 31, 1997. During a second call, Spencer alleges that Charles said, "Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough."

Spencer responded to the palace statement on Sunday as part of a BBC video interview, filmed at Althorp, the Spencer family's estate in Northamptonshire, England, where Diana is buried on an island in the middle of a lake.

So, why, almost three decades after Diana's death, is her brother sharing new revelations now?

Next year's 30th anniversary is certainly one factor — but not the only one.

In a press release issued last month by Penguin Random House, the book's publisher, Spencer was quoted as saying he'd been "inundated yet again with requests for interviews" about Diana, adding, "This has convinced me to write down my own thoughts and memories, once and for all, rather than having the discomfort of again reading the opinions of others, many of which are based on untruths that have become accepted over time."

He continued, "The aim of this book is to tell the truth about Diana from her brother's perspective, just as I attempted to do when speaking at her funeral."

Diana's official funeral ceremony took place at Westminster Abbey in London on Sept. 6, 1997. In his eulogy, Spencer insisted that Diana's memory would never be "extinguished," which he said on Sunday was intentionally worded following Charles's alleged insistence that Diana would be forgotten after her death. And this book appears to be reinforcing that promise to keep her memory alive.

In his BBC interview, Spencer presented himself as both a historian and Diana's brother. He said that he considered himself an "eyewitness to history" and described sharing what happened as his "duty" in the "final season" of his life. "Both of my parents died in their 60s and I'm in my 60s," he said. "I'm aware of mortality, and I wanted to just put things down once and for all that were true."

Spencer became emotional as he said he misses Diana "every day" and that sibling loss is something "you never get over."

Those explanations — the approaching anniversary, his desire to correct the record and his own awareness of mortality — answer the question of timing. But the book also reflects Spencer's long history with the institution his sister married into.

The rupture described by Spencer occurred during the second of two phone calls with Charles in the week of Diana's death — the only calls Spencer said they ever had. Spencer said he objected to William and Harry being expected to walk behind their mother's coffin at her funeral, believing that Diana would not have wanted her sons to be subjected to such scrutiny while grieving.

Spencer said Charles argued that he had walked behind the coffin of his mentor and great-uncle, Lord Mountbatten, but Spencer replied that Charles was an adult at the time and that Mountbatten wasn't his mother. That's when Charles "went ballistic," according to Spencer, and made the comment about Diana being forgotten.

Spencer told the BBC his account of the phone calls with Charles "will not be a surprise" to William and Harry.

At Diana's funeral, Spencer delivered a eulogy widely interpreted as a criticism of the British monarchy. In it, he said he would do all he could to ensure William and Harry were not "simply immersed by duty and tradition" and "recognize the need for them to experience as many different aspects of life as possible," while respecting and encouraging them in their royal role.

Despite his run-ins with the royals, Spencer told the BBC that he isn't anti-monarchy. In fact, he confirmed that he still supports the institution but wants it to be more modern.

Spencer has also strongly rejected the suggestion that he had included salacious material simply to sell books.

articles.title: 72nd National Film Awards explained: Why ‘Article 370’, ‘Bramayugam’, ‘Chandu Champion’ and ‘Stree 2’ are winning in 2026 for their 2024 film cycle?
articles.summary: At first glance, the 72nd National Film Awards may appear to be recognising films two years after their release. The ceremony is being held in Septemb.
articles.body: At first glance, the 72nd National Film Awards may appear to be recognising films two years after their release. The ceremony is being held in September 2026, while several of the films and performances receiving honours belong to 2024. This raises a natural question: why are the National Film Awards being presented so long after the films were released?The answer lies in the difference between the film eligibility year, the award edition, the announcement of winners and the actual presentation ceremony. The 72nd National Film Awards correspond to the 2024 film cycle, even though the winners were announced and the awards are being presented in 2026.The 72nd edition belongs to the 2024 film cycleThe simplest way to understand the timeline is to focus on the award edition and its eligibility period rather than the date of the ceremony. For the 72nd National Film Awards, films such as 'Article 370', 'Bramayugam', 'Chandu Champion', 'Amaran', 'Kalki 2898 AD', 'Stree 2' and 'Pushpa: The Rule Part-02' were considered as part of the 2024 eligibility cycle. The winners were announced on July 18, 2026, while the awards ceremony is taking place on September 22, 2026. Therefore, 2026 is the year in which the results are being announced and the honours presented; it is not the year being judged.Why is there a gap between the film year and the ceremony?The National Film Awards follow a formal selection process before the winners are announced. Films first have to meet the eligibility requirements for the relevant award cycle. For the 72nd edition, feature films needed to have been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification during 2024, along with satisfying the other prescribed conditions. Once eligible entries are submitted, they are evaluated by juries. Feature films go through regional panels before being considered by a central jury, while non-feature films and Best Writing on Cinema are evaluated through separate jury processes. The awards cover films from across India and multiple languages and categories. As a result, the jury process involves examining a large body of work before the final winners are selected.This multi-stage process is one of the reasons why the award presentation does not necessarily take place in the same calendar year as the films being honoured.Who selected the winners for the 72nd National Film Awards?The 72nd National Film Awards had separate juries for different sections.Filmmaker Jayaraj headed the Feature Film Jury, Aseem Sinha chaired the Non-Feature Film Jury, while A Chandrasekhar headed the Best Writing on Cinema Jury. Their respective assessments formed the basis for the winners announced in July 2026.From ‘Article 370’ to ‘Bramayugam’: Major winners from the 2024 cycleThe 2024 film cycle produced winners across acting, direction and several other categories. Article 370 was named Best Feature Film, while Yami Gautam won Best Actress in a Leading Role for her performance in the film. Mammootty and Kartik Aaryan shared the Best Actor in a Leading Role honour for 'Bramayugam' and 'Chandu Champion', respectively.Rajkumar Periasamy won Best Director for 'Amaran'.
